canonical_statement: The analysis evaluated gastrointestinal adverse events with once-weekly semaglutide 2.4 mg in adults with overweight or obesity and assessed their contribution to weight loss.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We evaluated gastrointestinal (GI) adverse events (AEs) with once-weekly semaglutide 2.4 mg in adults with overweight or obesity and their contribution to weight loss (WL).

canonical_statement: STEP 1, STEP 3 and STEP 4 enrolled adults aged at least 18 years with BMI at least 30 kg/m2, or BMI at least 27 kg/m2 with at least one weight-related comorbidity, and without diabetes.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: STEP 1, 3 and 4 enrolled adults aged ≥18 years with a BMI ≥27 kg/m2 (with ≥1 weight-related comorbidity) or ≥30 kg/m2, without diabetes.

inclusion_criteria: BMI >=30 kg/m2, or BMI >=27 kg/m2 with >=1 weight-related comorbidity

canonical_statement: STEP 2 enrolled adults with BMI at least 27 kg/m2 and type 2 diabetes.

population.label: STEP 2 participants

canonical_statement: Semaglutide was initiated at 0.25 mg once weekly for 4 weeks and escalated every 4 weeks to 0.5 mg, 1.0 mg, 1.7 mg and 2.4 mg at week 16; participants unable to tolerate 2.4 mg could remain at a lower maintenance dose with at least one attempt to re-escalate.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Each STEP trial included an initial dose escalation for semaglutide, with initiation at 0.25 mg once weekly for 4 weeks, increased at 4-weekly intervals to 0.5 mg, 1.0 mg, 1.7 mg and finally 2.4 mg at week 16.

exposures.details: Escalated every 4 weeks to 0.5 mg, 1.0 mg, 1.7 mg and 2.4 mg at week 16; lower maintenance doses allowed for intolerance with re-escalation attempt.

canonical_statement: STEP 1-3 used similar 68-week randomized placebo-controlled designs, enabling pooled post-hoc gastrointestinal adverse-event analyses of semaglutide 2.4 mg versus placebo.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Study designs were similar, consisting of a 68-week, randomized, placebo-controlled treatment period (Figure S1), enabling pooling of data.

canonical_statement: STEP 4 used a randomized withdrawal design after a 20-week open-label semaglutide run-in, and only participants tolerating semaglutide 2.4 mg at week 20 were eligible for randomization to continued semaglutide or placebo.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Only those who tolerated the 2.4 mg dose at week 20 were eligible for randomization.

canonical_statement: Adverse-event onset and end dates were collected throughout each trial using open-ended, non-leading verbal questions, followed at subsequent contacts, and coded using MedDRA version 22.1.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: AE information, including onset and end date, was collected throughout each trial, using open-ended, non-leading verbal questions.

canonical_statement: For pooled STEP 1-3 adverse-event analyses, on-treatment exposure was defined as trial product within the previous 49 days; percentages and event rates were adjusted using Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel weights, and median adverse-event durations were estimated using Kaplan-Meier methods.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The percentage of participants that experienced GI AEs and the event rate per 100 patient-years of exposure were adjusted using Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel weights to account for differences between trials. Median durations of GI AEs were estimated using the Kaplan-Meier estimator.

canonical_statement: The descriptive weight-loss analysis compared percentage body-weight change from baseline to week 68 among participants with versus without gastrointestinal adverse events who remained on treatment and had a week-68 weight assessment.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: A descriptive analysis of percentage change in body weight from baseline to week 68 among participants who did or did not experience GI AEs during STEP 1-3, using observed body weight data from participants who were on treatment and had a body weight assessment at week 68.

canonical_statement: The mediation analysis used a natural-effects model with imputation-based estimation to separate total body-weight effects into effects mediated by gastrointestinal adverse events and effects unrelated to those events.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Mediation analysis used a natural effects model with imputation-based estimation.

canonical_statement: The authors concluded that gastrointestinal adverse events with semaglutide 2.4 mg were common but typically mild-to-moderate, non-serious and transient, with few discontinuations, and that semaglutide-associated weight loss was largely independent of gastrointestinal adverse events.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: In conclusion, while GI AEs were common with semaglutide 2.4 mg ... effects were typically mild-to-moderate, non-serious and transient ... weight-lowering effects ... appeared to be largely independent of GI AEs.
